interest: Shows Japanese diaspora funding naval aircraft in Tsingtao, a blocked Ranger engine export to Kawasaki, and a 1939 air-strength survey.
keywords: Office of Arms and Munitions Control
overview: This file (decimal 894.348) consists of U.S. State Department, Navy Department, and War Department records from July 1935 to June 1940 relating to Japanese naval aviation equipment, foreign technology procurement, and operational deployments. The earliest documents cover the July 1935 presentation of a Type 90 scouting hydroplane ('Patriotic Service Airplane No. 83-TSINGTAO') donated to the Imperial Japanese Navy by the Japanese diaspora community in Tsingtao, China. The file also contains extensive late-1935 inter-agency correspondence between the State Department, War Department, Navy Department, and Ranger Engineering Corporation concerning the denial of export licenses and manufacturing rights for Ranger V-770-SG aircraft engines sought by the Japanese Navy and Kawasaki Dockyard Company on national defense grounds. Finally, the collection includes 1939–1940 intelligence records, notably reports on a second community aircraft presentation in Tsingtao ('Hokoku 379') and a detailed U.S. Military Attaché intelligence report from May 1940 tabulating the order of battle, aircraft complements, and base distribution of Japanese land- and ship-based naval air units across China, Taiwan, Korea, and Japan.

subfiles.about: Reports the formal naming and presentation of a Type 90 scouting hydroplane donated by the Tsingtao Japanese community to the Japanese Navy.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 40: Tsingtao's Japanese community donated a 'Patriotic Service' seaplane, accepted by Vice Adm. Hyakutake before 3,000 residents in July 1935.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 40 on Formal Designation of Airplane Presented to Japanese Navy by Tsingtao Japanese Community
subfiles.to: Nelson Trusler Johnson, American Minister, Peiping

subfiles.about: Photograph enclosure showing the Type 90 scouting hydroplane on Pier No. 2 during the Tsingtao presentation ceremony.
subfiles.summary: Photograph: the donated Type 90 seaplane on display at Tsingtao's Pier No. 2, beside an installed Shinto shrine.
subfiles.title: Photograph of Type 90 Scouting Hydroplane Presented to Japanese Navy (Enclosure 1 to Despatch No. 40)
subfiles.to: Nelson Trusler Johnson, American Minister, Peiping

subfiles.about: Transmits Ranger Engineering Corporation export license requests and conveys War and Navy Department objections on national defense grounds.
subfiles.from: Charles F. W. Wilson, Office of the Secretary of the Navy
subfiles.summary: Navy tells State it objects to exporting Ranger aircraft engines and a manufacturing license to Japan on military-secrecy grounds.
subfiles.title: Navy Department Letter Objecting to Foreign Sale of Ranger Engines to Japan

subfiles.about: Requests Navy permission to export one commercial Ranger V-770-SG engine ordered by Okura and Company for the Imperial Japanese Navy.
subfiles.from: Sherman M. Fairchild, President, Ranger Engineering Corporation
subfiles.summary: Fairchild asks the Navy to approve exporting a commercial Ranger engine ordered by Japan's Navy, arguing it differs from the classified US military version.
subfiles.title: Ranger Engineering Corporation Letter Requesting Export Clearance for Engine Ordered by Japanese Navy

subfiles.about: Requests clearance to export four V-770-SG engines and grant a manufacturing license to Kawasaki Dockyard Company in Japan.
subfiles.from: W. F. Davis, Chief Engineer, Ranger Engineering Corporation
subfiles.summary: Ranger's engineer argues its commercial engines for Japan's navy and Kawasaki differ from the classified US Navy version.
subfiles.title: Ranger Engineering Corporation Letter on Engine Export and Manufacturing License to Kawasaki Dockyard

subfiles.about: Inquires whether the War and Navy Departments' objection to exporting Ranger engines is specific to Japan or universal to all countries.
subfiles.from: R. Walton Moore, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Moore asks the Navy to clarify whether its objection to exporting Ranger engines to Japan is general or Japan-specific.
subfiles.title: State Department Inquiry to Secretary of the Navy Concerning Scope of Ranger Engine Export Objection
subfiles.to: Claude A. Swanson, Secretary of the Navy

subfiles.about: Transmits copies of Navy and State Department correspondence concerning the Ranger aircraft engine export application to the War Department.
subfiles.from: R. Walton Moore, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: State forwards the War Department a copy of its query to Navy on whether the Ranger-engine export objection is general.
subfiles.title: State Department Letter to Acting Secretary of War Regarding Ranger Engine Export Application
subfiles.to: Harry H. Woodring, Acting Secretary of War

subfiles.about: Clarifies that the objection to the export and foreign manufacture of Ranger V-770-SG engines applies universally to all foreign countries.
subfiles.from: Claude A. Swanson, Secretary of the Navy
subfiles.summary: Navy Secretary Swanson confirms the Ranger-engine export objection is universal, not specific to Japan.
subfiles.title: Navy Department Letter Confirming Universal Objection to Foreign Release of Ranger Engines

subfiles.about: Encloses for the War Department a copy of the State Department's formal letter to Ranger Engineering Corporation denying export approval.
subfiles.summary: State forwards the War Department its rejection letter to Ranger Engineering on the engine export application.
subfiles.title: State Department Memorandum to Acting Secretary of War Transmitting Rejection Letter to Ranger
subfiles.to: Harry H. Woodring, Acting Secretary of War

subfiles.about: Acknowledges the Navy's clarifying letter of November 23 and encloses a copy of the denial letter sent to Ranger Engineering Corporation.
subfiles.summary: State forwards the Navy its rejection letter to Ranger Engineering on the engine export application.
subfiles.title: State Department Memorandum to Secretary of the Navy Transmitting Rejection Letter to Ranger
subfiles.to: Claude A. Swanson, Secretary of the Navy

subfiles.about: Formally notifies Ranger Engineering Corporation that the U.S. government objects to the export and foreign licensing of V-770-SG engines.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Green, Chief, Office of Arms and Munitions Control
keywords: Office of Arms and Munitions Control
subfiles.summary: Green formally denies Ranger Engineering's export and licensing request for aircraft engines to Japan, citing military secrecy and national defense.
subfiles.title: State Department Refusal Letter to Ranger Engineering Corporation on Engine Export and Licensing

subfiles.about: Reports the presentation of a scouting seaplane ('Hokoku 379') and motor boat to the Japanese Navy funded by Tsingtao residents.

subfiles.to: Nelson Trusler Johnson, American Ambassador, Peiping

subfiles.from: William Mayer, Major, Field Artillery, Military Attaché, China
subfiles.summary: Report No. 9877: a detailed December 1939 tally of Japanese naval air units and aircraft strength across Korea, China, Hainan, Taiwan, and Japan, plus carrier and seaplane-tender air wings.
subfiles.title: Military Intelligence Report No. 9877 on Air Combat Operations: Distribution of Japanese Naval Air Units
